character_sheet: The Sea Monster is a plesiosaur: a front and back body block with four flipper fins, a six-segment neck rising to a small head of upper jaw, hinged lower jaw and two eyes, and a seven-piece tapering tail (ModelSeaMonster.createBodyLayer, ModelSeaMonster.java:72-168). It has 110 HP, 14 attack and 8 armour (MobStats.SEA_MONSTER, createAttributes SeaMonster.java:101-109), swims at 0.55 and crawls on land at 0.25 (aiStep :125-132), wanders far and looks about (:93-98), and every fifth tick takes its stored target or the nearest living thing in a 16-block box, closing to within four blocks plus half its width, raising the attacking flag and biting on a 1-in-4 roll (customServerAiStep :215-247; doHurtTarget :135-147 with a 0.6 knockback). Out of water it seeks the nearest water on a 1-in-25 roll and dries out slowly when it finds none (:194-213); in water it heals 1 on a 1-in-120 roll with a splash (:249-252). Cactus cannot hurt it, hits are refused for 8 ticks after each one and a mob attacker becomes its target (hurt :150-170). It spawns at night in the dark above y 50 with no other within 16 blocks (checkSpawnRules :339-346) in oceans and swamps (the ocean spawns and hostile_sea_monster biome modifiers). Read it as a long-necked swimmer: the tail's travelling wave drives it, the fins row, the neck rears and strikes.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (SeaMonsterRenderer.java:27, applied :36-40; shadow 1.0) on a 256x128 sheet (ModelSeaMonster.java:168); 1.25 x 2.5 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:154-156; the design's row writes [5,5] — the profile takes the registered size). The neck and tail are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) x the walking speed at the tip, divided by 7 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 3 / 2 / 1 from the base out, each segment placed at the end of the one before; zero below a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 unless the attacking flag is set (then the same wave, still scaled by the speed)
groups.plain: the tail sweeps side to side with the swimming or walking speed, the swing growing toward the tip
groups.math: a = (amount > 0.1 || attacking) ? cos(t * 1.3 * 0.5) * pi * 0.2 * amount : 0; TailBase.yRot = a/7; Tail2 = a/6; Tail3 = a/5; Tail4 = a/4; Tail5 = a/3; Tail6 = a/2; TailTip = a; positions along the chain by cos/sin x 10 / 7 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 5
groups.phase: a threshold of 0.1 on the walking speed, waived while the attacking flag is set
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x wingspeed 0.5 = 0.65 rad/tick: the natural period is 9.67 ticks

groups.name: fins
groups.amplitude: moving (speed above 0.1) or attacking: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) x the walking speed; still: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (3.6 deg); the front fins take the wave on both pitch (about −0.523) and yaw (about ±0.698), the back fins its negative
groups.plain: the four flippers row — the front pair and the back pair opposite — with the speed, and stir faintly at rest
groups.math: f = (amount > 0.1 || attacking) ? cos(t * 1.2 * 0.5) * pi * 0.2 * amount : cos(t * 1.2 * 0.5) * pi * 0.02; FinFrontLeft.xRot = f - 0.523, yRot = f + 0.698; FinBackLeft.xRot = -f - 0.523, yRot = -f + 0.698; FinFrontRight.xRot = f - 0.523, yRot = f - 0.698; FinBackRight.xRot = -f - 0.523, yRot = -f - 0.698
groups.phase: state-branching: the speed threshold or the attacking flag selects the speed-scaled stroke over the rest stir
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.2 x wingspeed 0.5 = 0.6 rad/tick: the natural period is 10.5 ticks

groups.name: neck
groups.amplitude: moving or attacking: a rise of 0.455 x the speed plus pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg) x the speed at 0.45 rad/tick; still: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (3.6 deg) at 0.15 rad/tick; the base takes a fifth about 0.455, then the segments add a quarter, a third and a half and take back a half and a third, each placed 9 (then 5) units up the one before; the head rides the last segment and turns half the look yaw
groups.plain: the neck rears and nods along its six segments, strongly with the speed or when attacking, faintly at rest; the head rides its end and follows the look
groups.math: n = (amount > 0.1 || attacking) ? 0.455 * amount + cos(t * 0.9 * 0.5) * pi * 0.25 * amount : cos(t * 0.3 * 0.5) * pi * 0.02; NeckBase.xRot = 0.455 + n/5; Neck2 = NeckBase + n/4; Neck3 = Neck2 + n/3; Neck4 = Neck3 + n/2; Neck5 = Neck4 - n/2; Neck6 = Neck5 - n/3; TopJaw / eyes placed 5 units past Neck6, yRot = look yaw x 0.5; positions along the chain by sin/cos x 9
groups.phase: state-branching: the speed threshold or the attacking flag selects the rearing wave over the rest breath
groups.omega_note: the classic phase moving is ageInTicks x 0.9 x wingspeed 0.5 = 0.45 rad/tick (period 14.0 ticks); still x 0.3 x 0.5 = 0.15 (41.9 ticks)

groups.name: jaw
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.17 = 0.534 rad (31 deg) about 0.45 at 0.85 rad/tick; not attacking: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad (9 deg) about 0.17 at 0.1 rad/tick
groups.plain: the lower jaw chomps wide while the attacking flag is set and breathes slowly otherwise
groups.math: BottomJaw.xRot = attacking ? 0.45 + cos(t * 1.7 * 0.5) * pi * 0.17 : 0.17 + cos(t * 0.2 * 0.5) * pi * 0.05 (placed with the head, yRot the look yaw x 0.5)
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (SeaMonster.java:49; set at :237 within reach, cleared at :245) selects
groups.omega_note: the classic phase attacking is ageInTicks x 1.7 x wingspeed 0.5 = 0.85 rad/tick (period 7.39 ticks); calm x 0.2 x 0.5 = 0.1 (62.8 ticks)

behaviour: Moving (a walking speed above 0.1) or with the attacking flag set, three speed-scaled waves run: the tail sweeps at 0.65 rad/tick (a 9.7-tick period), the swing growing from a seventh at the base to the full 36 degrees at the tip (ModelSeaMonster.java:175-194); the four flippers row at 0.6 rad/tick, front and back pairs opposite (:195-203); and the neck rears by 0.455 x the speed and nods 45 degrees x the speed along its six segments at 0.45 rad/tick, the head riding its end (:204-226). Still, the tail is straight and the fins and neck stir 3.6 degrees.

The head and eyes turn half the look yaw (:227-229); the lower jaw chomps 31 degrees at 0.85 rad/tick while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (SeaMonster.java:49, raised at :237 within four blocks plus half the target's width) and breathes 9 degrees at 0.1 rad/tick otherwise (:230-236).
The two body blocks are static; the walk position plays no part. The entity swims at 0.55 and crawls at 0.25 (aiStep :125-132), so the same waves run faster in the water.
The bite (doHurtTarget, SeaMonster.java:135-147) is rolled by the fifth-tick scan (:215-247) — nothing in the code fires an animation for it.

wishlist: in `swim`: the tail's travelling wave (ModelSeaMonster.java:175-194) at the water speed with the body undulating — the code moves only the tail, fins and neck, never the body blocks
in `walk`: a slow, dragging crawl on the flippers (the land speed is 0.25, SeaMonster.java:129) with the neck held low
in `aggro_idle`: the neck reared (the 0.455 x speed lift at :204-205 reads as a rear) and the jaw working (:231-232)
in `attack`: a neck strike down with the jaw's chomp; the bite lands within four blocks plus half the target's width (SeaMonster.java:235-239)
locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelSeaMonster row (geckolib_migration_design.md:452): 'TopJaw [2.5,1.5] @1; BodyFront/BodyBack [5,3.5] @0.5; NeckBase/Neck3/Neck6 [2,2] @0.5; four fins [2.5,0.7] @0.25; TailBase/Tail3/TailTip [1.5,1.5] @0.25'. Every named bone resolves as written (ModelSeaMonster.createBodyLayer); 'four fins' taken as FinFrontLeft, FinFrontRight, FinBackLeft and FinBackRight. The row writes the main size as [5,5] and the renderer scale as x3; the registration is 1.25 x 2.5 (ModEntities.java:154-156) and SeaMonsterRenderer.SCALE is 1.0 (SeaMonsterRenderer.java:27) — the profile takes the registered size and the owner reconciles the row.
